newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh and India withdrew their troops after two days of tension in Kulchibari border in northern Lalmonirhat district following a flag meeting on Sunday night.
A Bangladeshi national was killed on Monday when a mine planted by Burmese border security forces blasted in a deep forest of Waladong frontier in Cox's Bazar district.
Parliament begins its budget session on Tuesday afternoon.
The government has offered additional financial benefits to the workers of government-owned textile mills, willing to retire early.
Trade transit to India could yield Taka 4 billion for Bangladesh, said H.S. Kumbhat, cheif of a visiting trade delegation from India's Northeastern region.
Police continued their search for Syeed Iskander, a retired army officer and brother of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, in connection with assaulting two army intelligence personnel.
A 5.7 percent GDP growth rate is expected to be achieved in the current fiscal year ending June 30, Ministry of Planning said.
The government will undertake a 500 million credit programme to help boost the country's handloom sector. REUTER
